Spinor represents a distinctive approach to web preloading experiences. The project's core objective was to transform the traditionally mundane site loading phase into a captivating three-dimensional introduction that engages visitors from their very first interaction.

Leveraging three.js, we crafted an immersive 3D scene where visual elements are procedurally selected at runtime, ensuring that each page load presents a subtly unique composition. This dynamic variability keeps the experience fresh for returning visitors while maintaining brand consistency. The animation was carefully optimized to balance visual richness with performance, ultimately being seamlessly integrated as a custom module within a WordPress ecosystem. GSAP provided the timing precision needed to orchestrate the various animation sequences, while Sass and Webpack rounded out the build pipeline for maintainable, production-ready code.

The Winc project marked my deep dive into the world of native web components, presenting both a significant learning opportunity and a substantial technical challenge. The mission was ambitious: architect and develop a complete ecommerce platform from the ground up, built entirely on a component-based paradigm.

What made this project particularly compelling was the emphasis on creating a rich, animated user experience while maintaining complete modularity. Each component was designed as a self-contained unit with its own encapsulated animations, powered by GSAP for fluid, performant motion design. This architectural approach demanded the creation of an extensive component library—a comprehensive system capable of generating any conceivable content layout or page variation through flexible composition patterns. The result was a truly modular site where components could be mixed, matched, and deployed in countless configurations, all while preserving consistent animation behavior and visual polish throughout the entire shopping experience.

Being invited to create a visual experience for Honey Soundsystem's 10th anniversary celebration was both an honor and an exciting creative challenge. The project called for a dancefloor projection that would become an integral part of the live musical experience, responding and evolving alongside the DJ sets throughout the night.

Using three.js as the rendering foundation, I developed a generative geometric animation system that strikes a balance between visual simplicity and dynamic complexity. The core concept centers on mathematically-driven shape movements—geometric forms whose motions are governed by precise mathematical formulas, making them ideally suited for real-time audio manipulation. As music pulses through the sound system, incoming audio data directly influences the animation parameters, creating a living visual representation of the sonic landscape. This reactive relationship between sound and visuals transformed the static projection surface into a dynamic canvas that breathed in sync with the music, amplifying the immersive atmosphere of the celebration.

Chromaforge began as a personal passion project—an exploration into the intersection of code, mathematics, and visual art through procedural generation. What started as creative experimentation evolved into a fully-featured React web application that serves as a generative art studio in the browser.

The application empowers users to create endlessly unique, vibrantly colorful artworks through algorithmic processes. Each piece is procedurally generated, meaning no two creations are ever exactly alike. The interface provides intuitive controls for generating, fine-tuning, saving, and downloading these digital artworks. Color manipulation is handled through tinycolor, while GSAP adds smooth, engaging transitions throughout the user experience. Since its initial release, Chromaforge has grown into a complete print-on-demand service—a platform where users can not only generate their own distinctive artwork but seamlessly transform their digital creations into wearable pieces by having them printed on their garment of choice, bridging the gap between digital art generation and physical fashion.

View Project

Gap has been woven into the fabric of American culture since 1969, and this project was an opportunity to honor that legacy in a way that felt worthy of it. The brief called for an interactive application chronicling the brand's history—a piece of permanent installation work destined for the GAP museum at their San Francisco headquarters, where it would serve as a touchpoint between the company's storied past and the employees and visitors who move through the space every day.

The application was built to be as much an experience as it is an archive, guiding users through decades of cultural moments, iconic campaigns, and brand milestones through a series of richly animated, touch-driven interactions. GSAP provided the precision and expressiveness needed to bring each chapter of the timeline to life, while Webpack kept the build lean and performant for the demands of a permanent public-facing installation. The result is something that feels less like a corporate history and more like a living, navigable piece of the brand's identity.

The Nylas project presented a sophisticated challenge at the intersection of technical communication and motion design: translating a complex software platform's capabilities into a visual narrative that was both technically accurate and immediately comprehensible to a broad audience. The brief called for an immersive SVG animation module that would live within the Nylas WordPress site, functioning as an interactive explainer that could convey the depth and elegance of the platform's feature set in a way that static copy and diagrams simply could not.

The animation system was architected as a self-contained module, designed to integrate cleanly into the existing WordPress environment without disrupting the surrounding page infrastructure. GSAP served as the animation engine, providing the sequencing precision and performance characteristics necessary to orchestrate layered SVG elements across multiple synchronized timelines. Each animated passage was carefully choreographed to guide the viewer's attention through the product's core functionality—connections, data flows, and API interactions rendered as fluid, purposeful motion rather than abstract technical diagrams. The result is a presentation layer that elevates product communication, making sophisticated infrastructure concepts legible and compelling to developers and decision-makers alike.

Working with AT&T meant operating at scale—producing a high volume of animated banner ads and social videos for one of the most recognizable brands in the country. The work demanded a disciplined approach to motion design, where every animation had to feel polished and on-brand while adhering to the strict technical specifications of a wide range of ad platforms and social channels. GSAP drove the interactive banner executions, providing the precise timing control needed to choreograph layered text, imagery, and transitions within tight filesize constraints. After Effects handled the social video pipeline, where motion graphics needed to feel cinematic while remaining optimized for mobile-first viewing environments.

Beyond the creative work, a significant part of the engagement involved identifying and eliminating repetitive production bottlenecks. I designed and implemented automation workflows that streamlined the handoff between design assets and final deliverables, reducing the manual effort required to resize, reformat, and export creative variations across dozens of spec combinations. What had previously been a labor-intensive process of duplicating and adjusting files by hand became a largely automated pipeline, freeing the team to focus on the quality of the work itself rather than the mechanics of producing it.
